## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** With shadows off (the default), no functional change was found: popup margins, window sizes and input masks resolve to the same values as before. With shadows on, the reserved padding covers Qt's `RectangularShadow` extent, card interiors stay untinted, and colour resolution and live enable/disable behave as documented.

With shadows enabled, two layout issues were found near screen and window edges, plus smaller notes below.

### Popups near a screen edge move inward instead of clipping their shadow

`PopupCard` and the bar tooltip window now include the shadow pad and are anchored with `PopupAdjustment.Slide`. Quickshell sends the full padded window size to the compositor, and Hyprland slides a layer-owned popup that crosses the monitor box back inside it. When the existing edge clamp engages, the whole window moves, card included:

```text
shadows off   |<5>[ card ]                  card 5 px from the edge
shadows on    |[<-- 25 pad -->][ card ]      window must fit on screen,
                                             so the card shifts inward
default insets: left/right 25, top 19, bottom 31 (logical px)
```

(Conceptual sketch, not a screenshot.)

With default settings a clamped card ends up roughly 20 to 25 px further from the edge than with shadows off. This follows from Quickshell v0.3.1 and Hyprland v0.56.2 source; it was not observed at runtime. Affected in-tree popups are the tray menu, tray manage popup and media widget when they sit near an edge (for example the tray at the far end of a top bar, or on a left/right bar). Bar tooltips for the edge-most widget are affected the same way.

**Impact:** position only; input and content are unchanged. It contradicts `docs/theming.md` ("Physical screen edges still clip shadows") and the `PopupCard` comment about positioning the visible card.

**Suggested change:** either document that popups near a screen edge move inward by the shadow extent, or keep the card position and trim the pad on a clamped side so the shadow clips there.

### `MultiSelect` popup can be pushed up over its trigger

`MultiSelect` sizes its popup to `_availableBelow = windowHeight - anchorY - Style.space(12)`. With `[popups]` shadows on, the new `bottomMargin` is 31 with default settings. Qt's popup positioner moves a popup whose bottom crosses that margin, so a long list that fills `_availableBelow` is moved up about 19 px (31 - 12) and can cover the lower part of its trigger.

**Impact:** layout only, when shadows are on and the list is long enough to reach the window bottom. No in-tree plugin uses `MultiSelect` today; it is exported through `qs.Ui`.

**Suggested change:** subtract the effective bottom margin in `_availableBelow`, for example `Math.max(Style.space(12), bottomMargin)`.

**Stacked toasts:** toasts are 8 px apart, while the default shadow extends 19 px above and 31 px below each card. Each shadow's inverted mask removes only its own card's interior, so a neighbouring toast's shadow can darken the next card. This is only visible with translucent `[notifications]` backgrounds; defaults are opaque. A short docs note, or larger toast spacing when shadows are on, would cover it.

**Optional:** every `BorderSurface` now evaluates `Shadow.surfaceSpec("")` and holds an inactive `Loader`, even though an empty section can never enable a shadow. A base/head micro-benchmark of 2000 surfaces with shadows off measured creation at 21 ms vs 47 ms and a new ~24 ms re-evaluation on each shell.toml change. Returning early for an empty `shadowSection` would remove that cost.

**Optional test improvement:** `surface-shadow-render-test.sh` skips only when PySide6 is missing. With PySide6 installed but no X display, Qt's offscreen plugin cannot create the forced OpenGL context and Qt Quick calls `qFatal`, so the test aborts rather than skipping (source-confirmed, not executed). Probing for a usable GL context (or `DISPLAY`) before running would fix that. Separately, the `white(image, 200, 240)` check samples below the padded render area (which ends at y=231), so it cannot fail; a sample inside the pad would detect a clipped blur.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of all 32 changed files and of the dependencies they rely on (Qt Declarative 6.9 and 6.11 `RectangularShadow`, `MultiEffect` and popup positioner; Quickshell v0.3.1 popup anchoring and regions; Hyprland v0.56.2 popup positioning). Non-rendering QML engine checks of the production shadow files on Qt 6.11.2, `qmllint` on changed files (exit 0), and a base/head micro-benchmark, all in an isolated sandbox. No pixels were rendered, no live or nested desktop session was used, and the PR's own Node, PySide6 and acceptance tests were not run. Edge-slide, overlap and offset figures are computed from source.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments (plus one targeted follow-up to the GPT 6 Sol assessment), Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
